issues.section: Prepare for Week 2: check your Geant4 install
issues.quote: Source your Geant4 and ROOT environment and run: geant4-config --version
issues.problem: No page in the course explains how to install Geant4 11.4 with its datasets. week02 Lab refers back here ('Week 1, step 7') but this is only a check. A student without an install is blocked at Week 2.
issues.fix: Add an install page: Linux build from source (GEANT4_INSTALL_DATA=ON, GEANT4_USE_QT=ON), macOS (Homebrew/conda-forge), Windows via WSL2 Ubuntu, plus a conda-forge or Docker one-liner; link it from the FAQ, week01 and week02.

issues.section: 5 What Geant4 does for a muography project
issues.quote: A Linux or macOS terminal (cd, ls, editing a text file)
issues.problem: Windows users are not mentioned anywhere in the course (no 'WSL' or 'Windows' in any page). WSL2 needs specific notes: WSLg for the Qt/OpenGL viewer, working inside the Linux filesystem, opening the VRML/ROOT files from Windows.
issues.fix: Add a WSL2 section: install Ubuntu, build or conda-install Geant4 inside WSL, check that WSLg exists for /vis/open, keep projects under ~ not /mnt/c, open outputs via \\wsl$.

issues.section: Prepare for Week 2: check your Geant4 install
issues.quote: root-config --version ... 6.xx/yy  # a ROOT 6 release
issues.problem: The FAQ says weeks 2-8 and 11 need only Geant4 + Python (uproot), and ROOT is only for musrSim weeks. Asking for ROOT here makes people install it for no reason.
issues.fix: Mark root-config as optional (only for weeks 9-10).

issues.quote: SteppingAction adds each step's deposit to a running total kept by EventAction
issues.problem: The course never shows Geant4's built-in scoring: command-based scoring meshes (G4ScoringManager, /score/create/boxMesh, /score/quantity/energyDeposit or doseDeposit, /score/dumpQuantityToFile) or G4MultiFunctionalDetector with primitive scorers (G4PSEnergyDeposit, G4PSDoseDeposit). 'dose' and 'Gy' do not appear anywhere. For dosimetry users this is the most transferable tool in Geant4 and what GATE/TOPAS wrap.
issues.fix: Add a section (here or in week05) that reproduces the Lab 4 Edep with a scoring mesh and with a primitive scorer, then converts to dose in a water phantom.

issues.section: Production cuts: a range, not an energy
issues.quote: Geant4 does not produce a δ-ray, a bremsstrahlung photon or a positron as a track if it would travel less than the range cut (0.7 mm in FTFP_BERT).
issues.problem: Only one global cut is taught. No G4Region / G4ProductionCuts / /run/setCutForRegion, which is standard in any phantom or small-detector work. No EM physics options (G4EmStandardPhysics_option4, Livermore, Penelope), no G4PhysListFactory / PHYSLIST, no /process/em/ commands or step limits. Course-W06-f tells students to record 'any EM option' but EM options are never shown. QBBC/QGSP_BIC (the usual choices for hadron therapy) are not mentioned.
issues.fix: Add 6.x 'Regions and EM options': fine cuts in a region, opt0 vs opt4 on the same Edep/secondary census, and a list of which reference lists suit which domain.

issues.section: Production cuts: a range, not an energy
issues.quote: Nothing is thrown away, and particles that are produced are tracked down to zero energy.
issues.problem: In 11.4, G4EmParameters sets lowestElectronEnergy = 1 keV and lowestMuHadEnergy = 1 keV (G4EmParameters.cc lines 150-151); below that, particles are stopped and their energy deposited. Also, cuts apply only to processes like ionisation, bremsstrahlung and charged-particle pair production; photoelectric, Compton and conversion secondaries are made regardless of the cut by default (applyCuts = false, line 124).
issues.fix: Say 'tracked down to a low tracking limit (1 keV by default)' and list which processes use cuts, mentioning /process/em/applyCuts.

issues.quote: Below about 10 µm in plastic, lowering the cut no longer changes the e⁻ threshold.
issues.problem: The course's own table (code/week06/cut_thresholds_g4_11.4.json, also used in assets/week06.js) gives plastic e- thresholds of 14.5 keV at 10 um and 1.74 keV at 3 um. The 990 eV floor is only reached at 1 um. The answer 'Geant4 never produces secondaries below its 990 eV lower limit' is also too strong: the lower edge can be changed (/cuts/setLowEdge), and cut-independent processes ignore it.
issues.fix: Change to 'Below about 1-2 um in plastic' and reword the answer to 'the production-threshold table has a default lower edge of 990 eV'.

issues.quote: secondaries per event, by particle:   e- 2.387   gamma 1.358
issues.problem: The expected output is condensed. RunAction.cc prints a 'CPU time per event' line and one species per line, so 'grep -A4' returns different lines from those shown. The text then quotes a '12-fold' CPU change that the displayed output does not contain. The same applies to Run B ('by particle:' / 'by creator :').
issues.fix: Paste the verbatim program output, including the CPU line, or label the block 'condensed'.

issues.quote: Volume name does not match ("Counter" vs "counter"). The SD is never called; every efficiency is 0, with no error.
issues.problem: This contradicts week11 Course-W11-b ('Fault 3 is not silent in Geant4 11.4 ... fatal at initialisation (Run0053)') and the 11.4 source, where G4VUserDetectorConstruction::SetSensitiveDetector issues Run0053 FatalErrorInArgument when no logical volume of that name exists.
issues.fix: Rewrite Course-W05-c to match Week 11: fatal Run0053; the silent variant is an SD attached to the wrong existing volume.

issues.section: Students: run every branch and fill the symptom table
issues.quote: git checkout -q $b && cmake --build build -j4 > /dev/null
issues.problem: faultlab has no configured build/ directory, so 'cmake --build build' fails. If the student's week05 folder already has a build/, make_faults.sh copies it with 'cp -r' and commits it with 'git add -A'. Its CMakeCache.txt then points to the old source path and CMake refuses to use it.
issues.fix: In make_faults.sh, delete build/ and write a .gitignore before 'git add'. In the student loop, run 'cmake -S . -B build' once first.

issues.quote: Make this layout and paste each file. Open a file to see it.

issues.fix: Add a 'Download week NN code' button and a public repo with one tag per week.

issues.quote: Week 10's app is a complete template, with a messenger for pre-initialisation parameters, an SD keyed by copy number, a t1-style ntuple and a scan script.
issues.problem: Physics-track students who skip uSR lose the recommended template, and all candidate topics are muon topics. The index promises 'any virtual experiment', but there is no example outside muon physics (e.g. depth-dose in a water phantom). The page also does not say who the 'evaluator' is for a self-paced student.
issues.fix: Name Week 8's app as an equal template, add 1-2 non-muon example topics, and state how capstones are submitted and graded.

issues.quote: Where is my progress saved? Only in this browser, on this device.
issues.problem: No help channel (forum, email, office hours) is given anywhere, although the share sections say 'In the course group'. For a paid course this is the first thing I looked for.
issues.fix: Add a 'Getting help' FAQ entry and link it from every lab and common-errors box.

issues.quote: Write, build and run a Geant4 application: geometry, materials, a particle gun and a physics list.
issues.problem: There is no G4GeneralParticleSource (GPS), no variance reduction or biasing (G4GenericBiasingPhysics, importance sampling, splitting), and no phase-space sources. These are core transferable Geant4 skills for medical and shielding users. The course stops at G4ParticleGun.
issues.fix: Add GPS to week02 or week05, and an optional reading on biasing, so the 'transferable core' claim holds outside muon physics.

issues.quote: Hands-on lab · 40 min
issues.problem: 40 min to create 9 files by pasting, do a first CMake build and run 5 macros is optimistic for a basic-C++ student on a fresh install. 'About 2-3 h a week' undersells weeks 5, 11 and 12 (3-4 h on the pages themselves).
issues.fix: Raise the lab estimates, or provide the code download so the estimate becomes realistic.

issues.quote: G4Accumulable<G4int> fN0{0};
issues.problem: In 11.4, G4Accumulable is an alias of G4AccValue (G4Accumulable.hh); new examples use G4AccValue. The code still compiles.
issues.fix: Add a one-line note about the new name.
